records.title: 4L60E Transmission 3-4 Clutch Failure / Slipping
records.description: Avalanches equipped with the 4L60E automatic commonly lose 3rd and 4th gear due to 3-4 clutch pack burnout, a known factory weak point. The long fluid circuit feeding the 3-4 clutch leaks at the input housing (steel shaft galls the aluminum bore) and at the 2-4 servo, so the clutches slip, overheat, and burn. Symptoms are smooth 1-2 shifts but a flare/neutral feeling into 3rd, often with delayed engagement.
records.solution: Rebuild the transmission with upgraded 3-4 clutch frictions/steels, a new/updated input housing, forward and 3-4 clutch pistons, and resealed 2-4 servo; severe cases get a full remanufactured unit. Adding a transmission cooler helps prevent recurrence.

records.title: Brake Line Corrosion (Salt-Belt Vehicles)
records.description: Early Avalanches (1999-2003 GMT800 generation) are subject to steel brake line corrosion, especially in road-salt regions where flaking/scaling pipes can rupture and cause sudden loss of brake pressure. NHTSA investigated roughly 6 million 1999-2003 GM full-size trucks/SUVs including the Avalanche but closed the probe with no defect finding and no recall, instead advising owners to wash the undercarriage.
records.solution: Inspect brake lines for scaling/flaking; replace corroded sections or the full set with coated/stainless lines. Preventively, regularly wash the undercarriage in winter. Severe cases require full line-set replacement.

records.title: Cracked Dashboard (GMT900 Models)
records.description: Second-generation Avalanches built on the GMT900 platform are widely reported to develop spider-web cracks in the dashboard, typically starting around the passenger airbag seam and above the instrument cluster. Cracking usually appears after years of UV/heat exposure, and owners report it spreading progressively (audibly worsening over bumps). GM never issued a recall, and a multi-state class action (E.D. Michigan) was dismissed in GM's favor on appeal, leaving owners to pay for replacement.
records.solution: Replace the dashboard pad/panel assembly (dealer or aftermarket), or fit an aftermarket dash cap/overlay as a lower-cost cosmetic fix. There is no warranty/recall remedy, so most owners pay out of pocket or use a cover.

records.title: Erratic Fuel Gauge / Fuel Level Sensor Failure
records.description: The in-tank fuel level sending unit on GMT800 Avalanches wears out, producing erratic readings: the gauge sticks on full or empty, drops suddenly, or reads inaccurately. The cause is wear/contamination of the resistive card the sender wiper rides on, leading to intermittent contact (sulfur in fuel accelerates it). On dual-tank 8.1L trucks the problem can affect tank selection/readout as well.
records.solution: Replace the fuel level sensor; because it is integrated into the in-tank fuel pump module, most shops replace the complete pump/sender module (requires dropping the tank or removing the bed). Cleaning contacts is a temporary fix at best.
symptoms: Fuel gauge stuck on full or empty

records.title: Excessive Oil Consumption & AFM Lifter Failure (5.3L V8)
records.description: The 5.3L V8 with Active Fuel Management (AFM/cylinder deactivation) is prone to two linked failures: excessive oil consumption from worn piston rings and an AFM oil deflector that sprays oil at the cylinder walls, and collapsed/failed AFM lifters that can damage the camshaft. Burning oil fouls spark plugs and can trip low-oil shutdown commands; a failed lifter causes a ticking/knocking misfire. GM settled the Siqueiros class action ($150M) over the LC9 5.3L piston-ring defect for 2011-2014 vehicles built on/after Feb 10, 2011.
records.solution: For oil consumption, GM's TSB remedy involves replacing the AFM oil-pressure relief valve/deflector and often the pistons/rings; many owners delete AFM (range-disabler or PCM tune + delete kit) to prevent recurrence. For a failed lifter, replace the lifters (and cam if scored), commonly done alongside an AFM delete. Eligible owners can file under the Siqueiros settlement.
symptoms: Burning oil / low oil between changes

records.title: HVAC Blend Door / Mode Actuator Failure
records.description: The plastic HVAC temperature (blend) and air-delivery (mode) door actuators fail commonly on GMT800 Avalanches. Internal plastic gears strip or position sensors wear out, producing a repetitive clicking/ticking behind the dash and loss of temperature or vent control. On dual-zone systems one side may blow hot while the other blows cold regardless of setting.
records.solution: Replace the failed actuator (driver-side temp actuator is easy to reach; passenger/mode actuators may require glove box or partial dash removal). After replacement the system may need to recalibrate (pull HVAC fuse or battery briefly).
symptoms: No change in temperature with knob
One side hot, other cold (dual zone)

records.title: Instrument Cluster Gauge / Speedometer Failure (Stepper Motors)
records.description: First-generation (GMT800) Avalanches share the GM truck instrument cluster that suffers stepper-motor failure, causing gauges (speedometer, tach, fuel, temp, oil, voltage) to stick, read inaccurately, flutter, or go dead. The defect was widespread enough that GM agreed to a 2008 class action special-coverage settlement covering 2003-2005 GM trucks/SUVs including the Avalanche, extending coverage to 7 years/70,000 miles.
records.solution: Replace the stepper motors and rebuild the cluster (DIY or specialist board-repair service), or replace the cluster. Vehicles within the settlement window (7 yr/70k mi) could get free replacement; out-of-coverage owners typically use an aftermarket cluster-repair service for far less than a new cluster.

records.title: Unwanted Low-Speed ABS Activation (Corrosion) - Recall 05V379
records.description: Corrosion of the front wheel-bearing hub can contaminate/affect the ABS tone ring and wheel speed sensor, causing unwanted ABS activation when braking at low speeds (roughly 3-10 mph). This extends low-speed stopping distance and pulses the pedal unexpectedly. GM issued recall 05V379000 (Aug 2005, ~1.35M vehicles) but limited the remedy largely to salt-belt states, frustrating owners elsewhere who report the same symptom.
records.solution: Per the recall, dealers inspect/replace affected front wheel speed sensors / hub bearing assemblies. Out-of-recall vehicles are fixed by replacing the corroded front hub bearing assembly (which contains the wheel speed sensor) and cleaning/replacing the tone ring.
symptoms: ABS engages at low speed when stopping

records.title: Unwanted ABS Activation Increasing Stopping Distance
records.description: First-generation Avalanches (2002-2006) can experience unwanted ABS activation during normal low-speed braking. The antilock brake system activates inappropriately, causing a pulsating brake pedal and increased stopping distances when it should not be engaging. The issue is more likely in environmentally corrosive areas where road salt deteriorates the ABS wheel speed sensor wiring and tone rings. This creates a safety hazard as the vehicle takes longer to stop than expected during routine braking.
records.solution: Inspect and clean all four ABS wheel speed sensors and tone rings. Replace corroded sensor wiring or connectors. If the ABS module itself is faulty, replacement costs $600-$1,200. Applying dielectric grease to sensor connectors during brake service can prevent corrosion. In some cases, ABS module reprogramming at the dealer resolves the issue.
symptoms: ABS activates during normal low-speed braking
Pulsating brake pedal when it should not be pulsating
Increased stopping distances during routine stops
ABS warning light illuminated on dashboard
Grinding or buzzing noise from brakes during normal stops

citations.title: NHTSA Complaints - Avalanche ABS Issues

communityRecommendations.content: Clean the ABS wheel speed sensors and tone rings during every brake job. Corrosion on these components is the most common cause of unwanted ABS activation. Apply dielectric grease to all sensor connectors to prevent future corrosion. This is a $20 preventive measure that can save $1,000+ in ABS module replacement

records.title: 5.3L Vortec AFM Active Fuel Management Oil Consumption and Lifter Failure
records.description: The 5.3L Vortec V8 with Active Fuel Management (AFM/DOD) in 2007-2013 Avalanches suffers from excessive oil consumption and premature lifter failure. The AFM system deactivates four cylinders for fuel economy, but the AFM lifters have a coating that wears off prematurely, leading to collapsed lifters, bent pushrods, fouled spark plugs, and catastrophic engine damage. GM issued TSB 10-06-01-008A for oil deflector installation but never recalled the vehicles. Oil consumption of 1 quart per 1,000 miles is commonly reported.
records.solution: Monitor oil level weekly and top off as needed. For a permanent fix, perform an AFM delete which involves replacing the camshaft, all 16 lifters, and valley cover with non-AFM components ($2,000-$4,000 parts and labor). An AFM disabler device ($300-$500) can reduce the issue by preventing cylinder deactivation. Change oil every 5,000 miles with full synthetic.
symptoms: Oil consumption of 1 quart per 1,000 miles or more
Blue smoke from exhaust on startup or acceleration
Check engine light with cylinder-specific misfire codes
Lifter tick or knock noise from engine

citations.title: Chevy AFM Problem Years Explained - ChevyGuide
Another 5.3 with AFM bites the dust - GM Truck Club
GM 5.3L AFM Delete on 2007 Avalanche - Green Tractor Talk

communityRecommendations.content: An AFM disabler like the Range Technology AFM Disabler ($300) prevents cylinder deactivation and dramatically reduces oil consumption. This is the cheapest first step before committing to a full AFM delete. Pair it with 5,000-mile oil changes using full synthetic

Do NOT ignore excessive oil consumption on the 5.3L AFM engine. Running low on oil with AFM active leads to collapsed lifters, bent pushrods, and catalytic converter damage from oil fouling. Check oil level at every fuel stop. A full AFM delete ($2,000-$4,000) is the only permanent fix

records.title: Body Cladding Fading, Cracking, and Clip Failure
records.description: The first-generation Avalanche (2002-2006) features distinctive gray plastic body cladding that is prone to fading, cracking, and clip failure. The unpainted plastic panels that encircle the body deteriorate from UV exposure, turning chalky white and developing cracks. The clips holding the cladding in place become brittle and break, causing panels to loosen or detach. The cladding issues are cosmetic but affect vehicle appearance and can expose underlying metal to corrosion.
records.solution: Restore faded cladding with dedicated plastic restorer products (Solution Finish, Cerakote Trim Coat). Replace broken clips with new GM clips or aftermarket equivalents. For severely damaged cladding, replacement panels are available from aftermarket suppliers. Some owners choose to paint the cladding to match the body color for a permanent solution ($500-$1,500 for professional paint).
symptoms: Gray plastic cladding turning white or chalky
Underlying metal visible where cladding has pulled away

citations.title: Avalanche Cladding Issues - Chevy Avalanche Fan Club

communityRecommendations.content: Solution Finish or Cerakote Trim Coat are the best products for restoring faded Avalanche cladding. Apply every 6-12 months to maintain appearance. For a permanent fix, many owners paint the cladding to body color - this eliminates the fading issue entirely and modernizes the look

records.title: Dashboard Cracking Above Instrument Cluster and Airbag Panel
records.description: The 2007-2013 Chevrolet Avalanche (and related GMT900 trucks) suffers from widespread dashboard cracking. The upper dashboard material shrinks and cracks due to UV exposure and heat cycling, with cracks typically developing above the instrument cluster, over the passenger airbag panel, and at the windshield defroster vents. Over 100 complaints have been filed with NHTSA. There are safety concerns that dashboard fragments could become projectiles during airbag deployment in a crash.
records.solution: Dashboard replacement is the proper fix but costs $1,500-$2,500 installed at a dealer. More affordable options include dash covers ($50-$100), dashboard replacement kits ($200-$400), or professional dashboard repair services ($300-$600). A class-action lawsuit was filed but GM has not issued a recall.
symptoms: Visible cracks in dashboard above instrument cluster
Cracks appear primarily in sun-exposed areas
Dashboard surface becomes brittle and flaky

citations.title: 102 Complaints: Chevrolet Avalanche Dashboard Crack Problems
GM Cracked Dash Lawsuit & Recall Update

communityRecommendations.content: A quality dash cover ($50-$100) from DashMat or Coverlay is the most cost-effective solution. The Coverlay dashboard replacement panel ($200-$400) fits over the existing cracked dash and looks factory. A full dashboard replacement at a dealer is $1,500-$2,500 and rarely worth it on a high-mileage truck

Use a windshield sun shade when parked to slow dashboard deterioration. UV exposure is the primary cause of cracking. A quality ceramic window tint on the windshield also helps reduce UV damage to the interior

records.title: Reduced Engine Power Mode from Throttle Body and Pedal Sensor Faults
records.description: The 2007-2013 Avalanche frequently enters "Reduced Engine Power" mode, severely limiting acceleration. The most common causes are the electronic throttle body wearing out or the accelerator pedal position sensor (APP sensor) developing faults. The vehicle becomes barely drivable in this mode, struggling to accelerate to highway speeds. The issue can occur intermittently before becoming permanent.
records.solution: Diagnose with a scan tool to determine if the throttle body or accelerator pedal position sensor is the cause. Throttle body replacement costs $200-$400 parts and labor. APP sensor replacement costs $100-$250. A remanufactured throttle body from a quality source works well. Clear codes after repair and road test to verify.
symptoms: "Engine Power Reduced" or "Reduced Engine Power" message on dash
Vehicle struggles to accelerate past 20-30 mph
Check engine light with P2128 or P2138 codes
Intermittent power loss that resolves after restart

citations.title: Avalanche Engine Power Reduced Issues

communityRecommendations.content: P2128 and P2138 codes point to the accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor, not the throttle body. The APP sensor is a $50-$100 part and takes 15 minutes to replace. Do NOT let a shop sell you a throttle body without confirming the APP sensor is not the cause - it is the cheaper and more common fix

If the throttle body is confirmed bad, AC Delco remanufactured units are the best value. Aftermarket throttle bodies for the 5.3L are hit-or-miss. Clean the throttle body with CRC Throttle Body Cleaner before replacing - sometimes carbon buildup alone causes the reduced power mode
